mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI engine replacement typically costs between £2,200 and £3,800 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. OM642 V6 units range from £2,200 to £3,800 supply only. Rebuilt OM642 (Viano 3.0 / 3.5 CDI): £2,200-£3,800 supply only. Reconditioned units: £1,800-£3,200. Used engines from breakers: £1,200-£2,500 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £400-£800 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Viano 3.0 and 3.5 CDI OM642 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 diesel's most common failure is oil cooler seal degradation - the seals cost under £10, but accessing them requires 8-12 hours of labour. Oil cooler seals (A6421880480) fail between 70k-150k miles. Oil leaks from the inner-V of the engine - often dripping onto the bell housing. Mercedes Service Bulletin LI18.30-P-055434 covers this issue. If ignored, oil loss can lead to belt contamination and engine seizure.

mainEntity.name: Is the OM642 engine in the Viano 3.0 and 3.5 CDI reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 is fundamentally a strong, refined engine - but it has one significant weakness: the oil cooler seals. The engine block and internals are exceptionally durable. Oil cooler seal failure is predictable and expensive to repair. With preventative maintenance, these engines regularly exceed 200,000 miles. Many high-mileage OM642 Vianos remain in commercial and private hire service.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM642 oil cooler seal failure in a Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642's oil cooler seals typically show warning signs before complete failure. Oil spots on the driveway beneath the engine area. Burning oil smell from the engine bay - oil dripping onto hot components. Low oil level warnings between services. Oil residue visible in the inner-V of the engine (visible with inspection). If ignored, oil contamination of the belt tensioner can cause sudden failure.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., oil cooler seals, turbo inlet seal, EGR cooler). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic oil starvation. Oil cooler seal replacement at specialist: £800-£1,400 - catch it early. Turbo inlet seal replacement: £250-£450 - preventative maintenance. Full OM642 rebuild: £2,200-£3,800 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Given Viano 3.0 / 3.5 CDI values (£4,000-£12,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. Viano 3.0 CDI (2006-2010): OM642.990 (204hp). Viano 3.0 / 3.5 CDI (2010-2014): OM642.890 (224hp). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI. The OM642 V6's weight, W639 subframe geometry, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. V6 engine weight requires proper lifting equipment. Subframe must be lowered - not a driveway job. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation required. Specialist supply & fit costs £400-£800 - essential for a V6.

acceptedAnswer.text: Every engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty, with many specialists offering 24-month coverage on OM642 rebuilds. Marco Polo camper variant offered with same OM642.990 engine
W639 facelift introduces upgraded OM642.890 with 224hp (165kW), 440Nm torque, 5G-Tronic or 7G-Tronic transmission
Viano production ends, replaced by Mercedes V-Class

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz Viano 3.0 CDI / 3.5 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Viano 3.0 CDI and 3.5 CDI rely on the OM642 V6 diesel - a smooth and refined engine that delivers effortless torque, but has developed a well-documented reputation for specific, expensive failures. Oil cooler seal leakage is the dominant replacement driver, while turbocharger oil seal failure and EGR cooler cracking also feature prominently. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common Viano 3.0 and 3.5 CDI engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Failure - Why the Viano 3.0 / 3.5 CDI Leaks Oil
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler seals (A6421880480) sit deep in the "V" of the OM642 V6 engine between cylinder banks. These rubber seals degrade over time, allowing oil to leak down the back of the engine and onto the driveway. The seals themselves cost under £10 - but accessing them requires 8-12 hours of labour. A Mercedes Service Bulletin (LI18.30-P-055434) addresses this known issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of oil cooler seals, intake manifold gaskets, and related seals while accessible
repairOptions.longevity: 70k-150k miles; engine remains sound after repair

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit reconditioned OM642 with new seals, upgraded components, and warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if oil starvation has caused bearing damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W639 Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI is worth £4,000-£12,000 depending on condition and mileage - the full replacement cost of £2,200-£3,800 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £4,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: This is an expensive job for what seems like a minor leak - but it's a known, predictable failure on the OM642. Don't ignore it; oil loss can lead to belt contamination and eventual engine seizure. Use a reputable Mercedes specialist (£800-£1,400) rather than a dealer. If caught early with no engine damage, the seal replacement is the correct fix.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 engine prices for your Viano 3.0 / 3.5 CDI

problems.group: OM642 Turbocharger Oil Seal & EGR Cooler Failure
problems.h4: OM642 Turbocharger Oil Seal & EGR Cooler Failure - Power Loss and Emissions Faults
problems.rootCause: The OM642's turbocharger inlet seal can fail, causing oil leaks and potential turbo damage. The EGR cooler can also crack under thermal stress, leading to coolant loss and emissions faults - particularly on urban-driven vehicles. Turbo actuator sticking due to carbon buildup is also common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbo inlet seal, clean oil residue, inspect turbo condition
Replace EGR cooler, clean EGR valve, perform system reset
Supply & fit reconditioned OM642 with new turbo components and EGR system
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI worth £4,000-£12,000, turbo seal replacement at £250-£450 and EGR cooler replacement at £500-£800 are justifiable repairs. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: If you notice oil leaks from the turbo area or loss of power, have the turbo inlet seal and EGR system inspected immediately. The turbo seal is a relatively inexpensive repair (£250-£450) if caught early. For EGR cooler issues, specialist replacement is significantly cheaper than dealer pricing.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes Viano 3.0 / 3.5 CDI engine prices

problems.group: OM642 Swirl Flap & Intake Manifold Issues
problems.h4: OM642 Swirl Flap & Intake Manifold Issues - Why the Viano 3.0 / 3.5 CDI Loses Response
problems.rootCause: The OM642's intake port shutoff (swirl flap) system can fail, affecting EGR operation and causing loss of power and emissions faults. Carbon buildup in the intake manifold is common on vehicles used primarily for short journeys.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean intake manifold, swirl flaps, clear carbon deposits
Replace swirl flap actuator, new seals, recalibrate
Supply & fit reconditioned OM642 with new intake components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. For catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a Viano 3.0 or 3.5 CDI worth £4,000-£12,000, intake cleaning at £300-£500 is excellent preventative maintenance. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The OM642's intake system benefits from regular carbon cleaning, particularly on urban-driven vehicles. If you notice rough idle or loss of power, have the intake manifold and swirl flaps inspected. Specialist cleaning is significantly cheaper than dealer pricing and can restore lost performance.
